- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 2.0), model often overcorrects and underpredicts the next 5–7 days; apply a “lag correction” by adding 0.1–0.3 to forecast for 3–5 days post-spike.  
- Model consistently underestimates mean-reversion periods (e.g., after 1.9–2.0 range); add 0.05–0.15 to forecast for 3–7 days if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture long-term sentiment-driven drift; if sentiment is trending upward over 5+ days, add 0.1–0.2 to forecast for last 10 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings (e.g., +0.33, -0.33, +0.33), model tends to “smooth” extremes; apply a “sentiment asymmetry” rule: amplify forecast for +sentiment days by 5–10% and dampen for –sentiment days by 5–10%.
